# Branch per Experiment

A git branch holds **one hypothesis**, not one feature. The branch name states the hypothesis, the
diff against `master` is the experiment, and the checkpoints and logs on the branch are the result.
Nothing merges unless it wins; losing branches stay reachable as evidence of what was ruled out.

Confirmed in `IT Applications in Business and Commerce`, where an eight-person team ran a baseline
plus nine named branches against a PPO race driver — **ten branch reports, two code trees shipped**.
See [[proximal-policy-optimisation]] and [[it-applications-in-business-and-commerce]].

## The ten documented branches, one idea each

| Branch | Hypothesis |
|---|---|
| `master` | baseline PPO env + agent; straightness + progress reward, auto-gear by speed |
| `160speed` | push target speed; bigger speed reward, wall-brake |
| `160speed+stablesteer` | the above plus 10× steer-smoothness and traction control |
| `Reward_func_improvement` | *(named for a reward change that the tip commit does not contain)* |
| `gear_strategy_max_jerk` | move gear into the action space, reward jerk |
| `headless` | stable reward + headless TORCS + rpm-band gear reward |
| `parallel` | asyncio rewrite, ~9 concurrent TORCS instances for throughput |
| `piasecki/fix1` | one-line fix: `--updates` relative to the resumed checkpoint |
| `stable` | separate actor/critic trunks, danger/time-to-edge reward |
| `a.bhuiyan` | full rewrite: offline racing line + data-driven car model + residual PPO |

## What makes it work: the lineage is written down

Branches alone are not a method — a list of ten branch names six weeks later is archaeology. What
makes this legible is that `INDEX.md` records how ideas *descend* from each other:

> "**Gear ideas:** [gear_strategy_max_jerk] (raw jerk) → [headless] (rpm band) → [a.bhuiyan]
> (data-driven torque/shift map)."
> — IT Applications in Business and Commerce/project/docs/branch-reports/INDEX.md, 2026-07-10

Three branches, one problem, each one superseding the previous answer — the endpoint of which is
[[data-driven-gearing-over-hand-tuned-rpm-bands]]. `INDEX.md` also carries a "Recurring findings
across branches" section naming what *every* experiment kept hitting: the corkscrew S-section,
gearing, and episodes too short to complete a lap. That is the payoff the individual branches cannot
give you.

## And the honesty test: the branch that did nothing

The reports audit rather than advertise. `Reward_func_improvement` is named for a reward change and
does not contain one, and the report says so first:

> "Despite the branch name, the tip commit contains **no reward-function code change**. The only"
> — IT Applications in Business and Commerce/project/docs/branch-reports/Reward_func_improvement.md, 2026-07-10

A report set that will contradict its own branch names is worth reading. Compare
[[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]].

## The cost, visible here

Branches of a shared codebase that never merge mean as many copies of the environment wrapper
drifting apart, and `snakeoil3_gym.py` (605 lines) is duplicated verbatim between the two trees that
did ship. It also means the reward function has no single definition — four distinct formulations
exist across the branches, catalogued in [[reward-shaping]].

And it forced a second decision: with ten branches and a submission that takes code, which do you
ship? See [[ship-two-branches-not-all-eight]] — two trees plus the full report set covering the rest,
an instance of [[generated-audit-artifact]].

## Scope limit — do not over-generalise this

This is **one repository, and not one the user drove alone**: the branches carry six named authors
and the real git history lives in `Szymon1905/AI_racer_pytorch`, not in the ingested repo. The
elsewhere-analogue in this corpus is [[multiple-solutions-side-by-side]], where alternatives coexist
in directories rather than branches.
